description:
A `rules.toml` holding only custom rules silently switches off every default rule, so a malformed label is written and `jit validate` still exits 0.

## Background

The default rules (`label-format`, `namespace-registry`, `namespace-unique-<ns>`, `type-hierarchy-known`) apply in memory when `.jit/rules.toml` is absent. Once the file exists, only its rows apply. `docs/reference/labels.md` and `docs/reference/configuration.md` tell adopters to add allowed values, value patterns and required namespaces by authoring custom rules in `rules.toml`. A repository following that advice without copying the default rows loses all of them, with no finding.

Reproduction on a fresh `jit init` repository:

```bash
printf '[[rules]]\nname = "custom"\nseverity = "error"\nenforce = false\nassert = { label-value-pattern = { namespace = "priority", regex = "^(high|low)$" } }\n' > .jit/rules.toml
jit issue create --title x --description d --label BAD   # exit 0, label written
jit validate                                             # exit 0, "Repository validation passed"
```

`docs/reference/configuration.md` also says the next jit-driven config write, `jit config set` or re-init, writes the matching rows through to `rules.toml`. `jit config set validation.strictness loose` on that repository exits 0 and adds no row.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: On a repository whose `rules.toml` holds only custom rules, a label violating `label-format` is refused or reported exactly as on a repository holding the default rows, and `jit validate` does not exit 0 over it.
- [hard] REQ-02: Removing a default row from `rules.toml` has one documented effect, and that effect is what the binary does.
- [hard] REQ-03: `docs/reference/configuration.md` and `docs/reference/labels.md` state what a config write does to `rules.toml`, and `jit config set` does exactly that.
- [hard] REQ-04: A test owns each of the behaviors above, on a repository built in storage the test owns.

## Notes

- Related: `jit validate --fix` refuses a `rules.toml` holding default rows whose schemas are absent (`captured image has no schemas/default-label-format.json`), while a custom-only file lets it write them. Converting `research` needed `--fix` with custom rows first, then the full file.
- Exposure on 2026-11-01: none. gf2, mealie-fi, inflected-messages and just-in-time each hold every default row their config derives. `research` holds them since its format 3 commit `9c581bd`.
- Reachable by following the shipped docs, so this decides what validation checks for an adopter.
title: Keep default rules in force when rules.toml holds only custom rules
